0882a35561cf45bfc3aaa61bed233ad64eef8806.summary: The report describes Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters (SLSH), a collective launched in August 2025 that brings together Scattered Spider, LAPSUS$ and ShinyHunters. It covers social engineering and vishing, MFA bypass, supply-chain breaches via Salesloft Drift, Gainsight and Zendesk, a Salesforce data-theft campaign, the ShinySp1d3r ransomware-as-a-service, attacks on UK retailers and Jaguar Land Rover, a claimed insider at CrowdStrike, and law enforcement actions. Many figures are the group's own claims or third-party estimates.

Resecurity researchers believe the groups will continue under different names; the group itself keeps its status deliberately ambiguous.
Loss figures for several attacks are given as estimates, and the report notes undisclosed payments make the extortion total unreliable.

08f94fedfd18aae263a8c97b5e95f0228ca6f439.summary: Rapid7 analysed an April 2026 enterprise intrusion that began with a message from a fake 'IT Support' account in Microsoft Teams. The attacker delivered a portable Python payload, which Rapid7 linked to the ModeloRAT framework. The intruder then escalated to SYSTEM using CVE-2023-36036, deployed a fake Windows lock screen to harvest a domain password, moved laterally, and likely exfiltrated a memory dump via an anonymous file-sharing service.

087dc70ebd1f683f17566d80eb7a5fce036d6570.summary: Article reporting that Google Cloud's Mandiant Consulting observed no new intrusions by Scattered Spider (UNC3944) after UK arrests of alleged members, and warned that UNC6040 uses similar social engineering. The author argues Scattered Spider and ShinyHunters may now be one group, citing a ShinyHunters leader's claim. It also describes two atypical incidents: repeated PowerSchool extortion demands in May, and an affiliate's Salesforce-related breach of a major health insurer despite a healthcare ban. Mandiant and others still use the separate names.

0862fc27df0a2f1e905022e214d6071621e9d315.summary: BleepingComputer reports that the Clop ransomware gang listed Saks Fifth Avenue on its leak site, as part of Clop attacks exploiting the GoAnywhere MFT flaw CVE-2023-0669. Saks says mock customer data was taken via vendor Fortra, with no real customer or payment card data, but did not say whether corporate or employee data was affected. Clop had earlier claimed 130+ organisations were breached in ten days.
